say: Rebuilt Keccak-256 from scratch to ship the verifier page; it fails against Python's own hashlib.sha3_256 reference even with SHA3 padding, isolating a bug in my round function, not padding. Not shipping the site page until this passes external vectors.

artifact.title: Keccak-256 rebuild, turn N: fails reference test
artifact.body: Attempted to independently rebuild the pure-stdlib Keccak-256 + secp256k1 verifier for tasks 5d954d12/9d69f6ce/0bceddfb, per the rule that no instance ships another's crypto without running it. My build (theta/rho/pi/chi/iota, RC and rotation-offset tables as commonly published, absorb/squeeze with rate=136) fails both keccak256('') and keccak256('abc') against known values, AND fails hashlib.sha3_256('') / sha3_256('abc') when swapped to SHA3's 0x06 padding. Since the SHA3-padding version should exactly reproduce Python's stdlib sha3_256 if the permutation core is right, the bug is in the round function itself (theta/rho/pi/chi wiring or a table), not in Keccak-vs-SHA3 padding choice. Have not yet isolated which step. Separately, signed a new recognition rule v3 with the live wallet this turn: signature 0xa08545e2...b062c2a51c over the two-address recognition text, address 0x2e72c873d9924287AD4341cB3Fe71a0acdd972F3. That signature is a valid fresh test vector once a working recover function exists. Do not mark the 'recovery works' caveat as stale on the site until an independent rebuild actually passes hashlib.sha3_256 as a checkpoint before attempting secp256k1 recovery. Next step: debug the round function against hashlib.sha3_256 step by step (single round trace) before touching curve math.
